items.question_text: The same heater warms 1 kg of water and 1 kg of cooking oil for the same time. The oil gets hotter. Why?

options.a: Oil has a lower specific heat capacity than water
options.b: The heater has more power when it heats oil
options.c: Oil stores more energy for each degree it warms
options.d: Water loses its energy to the air more quickly

feedback.b: The heater has the same power whichever liquid it heats.
feedback.c: That would make the oil warm more slowly, not faster.
feedback.d: Both lose some energy to the surroundings; that is not the main reason.

misconception_map.c: slip: reversed the meaning of heat capacity
misconception_map.d: slip: blamed dissipation for a heat-capacity difference

items.explanation: The same energy is supplied to each. Oil needs less energy per kg per degree (a lower specific heat capacity), so its temperature rises more.

items.stem: A [[machine]] transfers \([[E]]\,\text{J}\) of energy in \([[t]]\,\text{s}\). Calculate its power.

feedback.multiplied: This multiplies energy by time. Power is the energy transferred each second: \(P = \dfrac{E}{t} = \dfrac{[[E]]}{[[t]]}\).
feedback.upside-down: This divides the time by the energy. Power = energy ÷ time: \(P = \dfrac{[[E]]}{[[t]]}\).

sample_instances.question_text: A winch transfers \(15000\,\text{J}\) of energy in \(30\,\text{s}\). Calculate its power.

wrong.misconception: This multiplies energy by time. Power is the energy transferred each second: \(P = \dfrac{E}{t} = \dfrac{15000}{30}\).
This divides the time by the energy. Power = energy ÷ time: \(P = \dfrac{15000}{30}\).

items.question_text: Which statement about power is correct?

options.a: A more powerful machine always transfers more energy
options.b: Power is the rate of energy transfer, in joules per second
options.c: A powerful machine never wastes any energy at all
options.d: Power and energy are always measured in the same unit

feedback.a: A more powerful machine transfers energy faster, but not necessarily more in total.
feedback.c: Every machine dissipates some energy, however powerful.
feedback.d: Power is measured in watts and energy in joules.

misconception_map.d: slip: confuses the units of power and energy

items.explanation: Power is the rate at which energy is transferred: 1 W = 1 J/s.

items.question_text: Two pumps fill tanks on a farm. Pump P transfers 6000 J of energy in 20 s. Pump Q transfers 9000 J of energy in 45 s. Which statement is correct?

options.a: Pump P has the greater power, because it transfers more energy each second
options.b: Pump Q has the greater power, because it transfers more energy altogether
options.c: The pumps have equal power, because the energy and time are both larger for Q
options.d: Pump Q has the greater power, because it runs for a longer time

feedback.b: Power is not the total energy: it is energy per second. Pump P: 6000 ÷ 20 = 300 W; pump Q: 9000 ÷ 45 = 200 W. So P has the greater power.
feedback.c: Both numbers are larger for Q, but not in the same proportion. Pump P: 6000 ÷ 20 = 300 W; pump Q: 9000 ÷ 45 = 200 W.
feedback.d: Running for longer does not raise the power. Power = energy ÷ time: pump P is 300 W and pump Q is 200 W.

misconception_map.c: slip: assumed both quantities grew in proportion without calculating
misconception_map.d: slip: thinks a longer time means a greater power

items.explanation: Power = energy ÷ time. Pump P: 6000 ÷ 20 = 300 W. Pump Q: 9000 ÷ 45 = 200 W. Pump P transfers more energy each second, so it has the greater power, even though Q transfers more energy in total.

items.stem: A [[machine]] has a power of \([[P]]\,\text{W}\). How long does it take to transfer \([[E]]\,\text{J}\) of energy?

feedback.multiplied: This multiplies energy by power. Rearrange P = E ÷ t to \(t = \dfrac{E}{P} = \dfrac{[[E]]}{[[P]]}\).
feedback.upside-down: This divides the power by the energy. The time is energy ÷ power: \(t = \dfrac{[[E]]}{[[P]]}\).
